title: Classify full anchor boxes for positive unit metric triples (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written algebraic proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
D = diag(a,b,c), a,b,c positive rational 2-adic units
universal full canonical anchor retention <=> a=b=c modulo four
all other unit residue patterns => an explicit four-row factor with box=3
```

This answers the unit-domain part of JoyboyBrian / [PR5213](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5213)'s arbitrary-diagonal-triple opening. Its third weight can vary independently. For example, diag(1,3,5) has the exact four-row obstruction in the README, while diag(3,7,11) has full retention for every admissible factor. The proof preserves original whole-instance anchors and credits PR5213's one-parameter classification, Sagar Thakrar / PR3612's modulo-four coloring and F/O/L labels, Nick Petalas / PR5172's fixed obstruction, Aaron Wang/navinor and the retained F-star lineage. No predecessor theorem is audited or claimed as new. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19372203). Canonical base is 7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority revision 8. Seven new files under research/unit-metric-triples only.

## Evidence

- Before: PR5213 classifies diag(1,d,1) and explicitly leaves arbitrary positive diagonal triples open. After: PROOF.md gives the exact criterion for every positive unit triple, with a complementary four-row family and an attaining three-row witness.
- All 216 ordered metric triples from {1,3,5,7,1/3,3/7}: 54 admitted triples give 810 full witnesses on 13,446 rows. Literal normalized-factor checks preserve the original anchors, including negative column valuations and inactive columns.
- All 162 complementary triples have the independently enumerated box histogram (1,24,288,1296,0). The complete finite enumeration covers 5,952,690 ordered supported-label assignments, with six additional coordinate permutations. All 21 semantic and input-contract controls pass.
- Both registered warning-strict normal and optimized commands pass on CPython 3.12.15. The directly timed commands take 4.91 s and 4.74 s locally, below their 120-second limits. Metadata, whitespace, in-memory source compilation, committed bytes and source ancestry pass.
- Official seven-file export and declared-input coverage pass. Read-only Git-free normal and optimized replays with an empty PATH produce exactly the same generated hash-bound receipt as local replay. No receipt is handwritten; the verifier emits it on stdout.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/unit-metric-triples/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/unit-metric-triples/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/unit-metric-triples
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/unit-metric-triples --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 path may replace the absolute path. Expected markers are PASS_UNIT_METRIC_TRIPLES, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. Only the standard library is required; no predecessor code is imported or scientifically replayed. SOURCES.json pins exact proof provenance; all declared source commits are ancestors of publication.

## Limitations

The theorem assumes all three metric coefficients have valuation zero. Unequal valuations, unrestricted asymmetric F-star, physical decoder realization and complete paid/productive costs remain outside scope. Native owners, dirty restoration, routing, precision/tapes, stock, compiler and outer multiplication obligations are not discharged. No Lean, Docker, selected operator cold replay, independent human acceptance or formal proof-kernel review is claimed. The fixed finite implementation bounds and Python allocation deviation are documented in the README; the written theorem has no finite row bound.

## Open next questions

- Classify positive diagonal triples with unequal valuations. Start from dual column power-of-two scaling and preserve the original canonical anchors; the unit proof alone does not settle that domain.
- Bind an admitted unit metric to one actual weighted decoder and price every physical operation, target and restoration. No such source-owned supplier is supplied here.

## Related open work

At completion, refreshed open-PR searches and the newer contributions from this account identify no other PR studying this positive-unit canonical-box classification. PR5213 and PR3612 are merged predecessors. Main-tree, merged-PR and live-claim searches found no duplicate in their coverage; sparse local notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain limits.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/unit-metric-triples)`, passed at exact head `46977753900758487d30e37d2de9fa2d81ffb05f` in [run 41625234433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41625234433). The package replay runs both registered normal and optimized commands. Local metadata, committed-byte/source-history and read-only Git-free export checks also pass. Hosted execution is separate from independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** isolated.

Only one new self-contained research package is added. Shared code, frozen predecessors and the selected frontier are unchanged.
